post_commit_telemetry.description: HTTP handlers emit ordinary audit after mutation; stdout/file/SQLite/PostgreSQL request sinks remain optional/bounded asynchronous telemetry. Some CLI/startup operations only print or trace. security_outbox has a bounded read API, but no production dispatcher with persisted consumer cursor exists.

operator_output.description: One-shot operator command prints bounded result or report; it does not dispatch durable authority events. Existing outbox rows are separate from that output.

unsupported_no_delivery.description: No corresponding gateway-owned operation/delivery is shipped in this mode; required authority-event delivery cannot be inferred from provider audit or future plans.

groups.boundary: persist_policy_mutation -> PolicyControlPlane::commit -> commit_policy_in / postgres_documents::commit_in; active row lock and expected ETag guard; document/history, shared revision, active pointer and security_outbox commit together. Discovery acceptance invokes commit_policy_in inside its suggestion transaction.
groups.record: Immutable policy_documents retain actor, diff/action, document ETag and version. security_outbox retains committed revision/from/to; history is already an atomic record.
groups.actor: actor_user_id retained per document; issuer/auth method and an unambiguous operation identity are not captured by the shared commit request.
groups.identity: Version + deployment-scoped security revision identify committed authority; diff_summary carries handler action (including rollback). No persisted client operation/idempotency ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2: add scoped actor and stable operation/event identity at the existing document transaction boundary; preserve suggestion transaction composition. PR3: delivery cursor and retention contract.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: persist_to_file writes temporary file and renames; reload swaps runtime; append_policy_version_after_commit writes a separately configured SQLite history database afterward.
groups.record: Policy file survives successful persistence; SQLite policy history is separate and may fail after success. Neither optional telemetry nor the separate history write is an atomic authority/evidence boundary.
groups.actor: History has actor_user_id if append succeeds; file has none.
groups.identity: File semantic ETag; independent SQLite history version. No common authoritative revision or operation ID across commits.
groups.follow_up: PR4 depends on #242: introduce/reuse its crash-safe standalone revision ledger, bind file digest + activation + history + evidence, recover interrupted activation; keep required-durability policy mutations unsupported until proven.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: File watcher/SIGHUP -> reload_policy_from_file_locked validates file and replaces process snapshot, then emits reload telemetry; it does not append policy history.
groups.record: Operator-owned file and process snapshot; no atomic activation/evidence record.
groups.actor: Reload event does not authenticate an editing operator.
groups.identity: No ledger revision binds the accepted file to activation or identifies the operation.
groups.follow_up: #242/#425 PR4 must route watcher, SIGHUP and startup activation through the same ledger as admin publication; testing only admin endpoints is insufficient.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: Config rejects POLICY_FILE in PostgreSQL mode; replicas install authoritative database revisions.
groups.record: No file authority is supported in this mode.
groups.actor: Not applicable.
groups.identity: Security revision belongs to database publication, not a file reload.
groups.follow_up: Keep this operation refused; do not introduce a local file authority fallback.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: register_tools_via_control_plane -> commit_tools -> shared document transaction with CAS, name reservations, immutable version, pointer, revision and outbox.
groups.record: tool_documents retain actor and action/diff with version and ETag; outbox is atomic. A later failed local install does not undo that commit.
groups.actor: actor_user_id per immutable version; no issuer/auth method.
groups.identity: tools version and security revision, action openapi_tools_registered; no operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2: extend shared document contract once for policy/tools; preserve tool-name locks and committed-but-not-locally-installed semantics.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: Admin publication calls registry replace_local_definitions_with_persist with fs::write, then installs definitions. File watcher/SIGHUP reloads definitions into the registry and emits loaded telemetry without a history transaction.
groups.record: Tools file holds current document; no durable publication history/evidence transaction.
groups.actor: Authenticated actor only in separate telemetry.
groups.identity: Current tools ETag; no durable operation or history revision.
groups.follow_up: #242/#425 PR4: include tools-file writes and watcher/startup paths in ledger integration; current fs::write must not be described as an atomic evidence transaction.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: PostgresConnectionStore::create/replace locks shared Connection state, checks collection/object CAS, writes records, credential bindings, immutable version, shared revision and outbox in one transaction. Credential/TLS revisions derive from replacement.
groups.record: connection_versions actor/diff and outbox from/to are atomic; history cascades when Connection is deleted.
groups.actor: actor_user_id retained while parent exists; issuer/auth method absent.
groups.identity: Connection ID, connection/credential/TLS revisions and shared revision. Identical replace is a no-op; no operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2: preserve safe per-operation evidence independently of cascading Connection history; record credential changes by Connection identity/revision only, never binding IDs or locators.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: SqliteConnectionStore::create/replace uses an Immediate transaction for record and binding updates, then control plane publishes runtime snapshot.
groups.record: Current records and revisions are atomic; no per-mutation actor/history event is stored by these methods.
groups.actor: SQLite ConnectionStore create/replace accept no actor; admin handler emits actor separately.
groups.identity: Connection ID and per-axis revisions; no immutable operation identity.
groups.follow_up: PR4: append bounded evidence in the same Connections SQLite transaction; no separate audit database commit. Wire actor context through the managed-store adapter.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: delete checks ETag and dependencies, appends outbox tombstone to_version=0, releases names, deletes parent and commits.
groups.record: Outbox tombstone remains; connection_versions and bindings cascade. Existing durable deletion record already names resource and prior revision.
groups.actor: delete accepts _actor_user_id but does not persist it; attribution exists only in post-commit audit emission.
groups.identity: Shared revision, Connection ID, previous version and deletion sentinel; no operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2 first narrow storage slice: retain deletion actor/action/event identity in existing transaction without changing outbox tombstone semantics; test evidence survives parent cascade and rolls back on failed CAS.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: SQLite Immediate transaction checks dependencies and ETag, then deletes current record and cascades children.
groups.record: No durable tombstone/event after successful deletion.
groups.actor: No actor parameter at SQLite delete boundary; post-commit audit only.
groups.identity: Response uses prior Connection identity/revision; deleted record cannot reconcile an ambiguous response.
groups.follow_up: PR4: non-cascading tombstone evidence in the same Connections database transaction; test after restart and dependency/CAS rejection.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: MCP/OpenAPI replacements and overlay updates share Connection-state transaction and revision/CAS checks; entries, reservations, dependencies and outbox commit together. Includes scheduled refresh through store methods.
groups.record: Current catalogs/overlay actor fields and catalog-specific outbox revisions; replacing catalogs deletes old rows and deleting Connection cascades them.
groups.actor: Actor supplied to catalog writers; replaced/deleted current rows do not retain historical actor linkage.
groups.identity: Connection ID, catalog revision (distinct from specification revision), shared revision; no operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2: preserve actor/action/revision evidence before replacement/cascade, including system refresh attribution; keep catalog outbox resource_type and version axis unchanged.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: Immediate SQLite catalog transaction checks Connection/catalog/overlay CAS and writes catalogs, dependencies and overlay together.
groups.record: Current catalog revisions/entries; overlay retains current actor, ordinary catalog replacement has no immutable actor/event history.
groups.actor: Admin telemetry and current overlay actor cannot establish actor for every retained historical change.
groups.identity: Connection/catalog/overlay revisions; no common operation ID or durable deletion evidence.
groups.follow_up: PR4: append evidence within the catalog transaction, including scheduled refresh and overlay removal; exclude enum-value refresh and status observations unless they change publication authority.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: LocalSecretStore create/rotate/delete and reencrypt_batch use Immediate transactions in Connections SQLite; control-plane preflights and runtime publication surround rotation. CLI reencrypt executes one bounded batch.
groups.record: Current sealed record, version and timestamps; rotation replaces material and deletion removes it. Key re-encryption updates envelopes without semantic credential-version change.
groups.actor: Local secret store methods accept no actor; HTTP audit follows write, CLI emits safe counts only.
groups.identity: Secret version is current state, not safe exported resource identity; no durable operation/event identity.
groups.follow_up: PR4: atomic non-secret event metadata in the same SQLite store; use generated event/operation identity and safe Connection linkage where allowed, never secret ID/binding/locator/ciphertext/key ID. Re-encryption needs batch operation evidence, not fake credential revision bumps.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: Configuration rejects local secret keyring in PostgreSQL mode; no shared local-secret table.
groups.record: No gateway-owned secret-value mutation.
groups.actor: Not applicable.
groups.identity: Not applicable.
groups.follow_up: Keep local-secret administration unavailable in cluster mode; external provider rotation is a separate authority and cannot share the gateway transaction.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: External operators/providers own secret-value rotation; GreenGateway resolver reads versions/material after authorization and preflight. Gateway changes to a binding belong to credential.binding_change.
groups.record: No gateway transaction can atomically commit a provider's independent rotation.
groups.actor: Provider-owned audit linkage; no authenticated gateway actor for an out-of-process rotation.
groups.identity: Provider-specific resolution versions are runtime cache inputs, not a gateway operation ledger.
groups.follow_up: Document external evidence correlation and provider ownership; do not claim gateway-required durability for provider writes or export locators into gateway evidence.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: create locks token resource state, inserts token, advances shared revision/high-water and appends outbox in one transaction.
groups.record: Token created_by/created_at and immutable create outbox revision survive token rotate/revoke; raw token never stored in event/outbox.
groups.actor: created_by retains creating subject; issuer/auth mode absent.
groups.identity: Token ID and row revision 1 plus security revision; no operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2: retain scoped creator/action/event identity at existing create transaction; returned plaintext must not enter evidence.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: SQLite INSERT persists hashed token and creator; async adapter delegates to that store.
groups.record: Current token row retains creator/time; no independent authority-event record.
groups.actor: created_by only, not issuer/auth context.
groups.identity: Token ID; SQLite token rows do not expose PostgreSQL shared/row revision counters.
groups.follow_up: PR4: wrap token insert and bounded evidence in one SERVICE_TOKEN_SQLITE_PATH transaction; no audit database dual write.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: rotate/revoke serializes token state/row, changes token row, reserves revision and appends outbox in one transaction. Repeated revoke does not advance revision or emit another outbox row.
groups.record: Outbox revision chain is already durable. Token row keeps creator, current revision and latest revoked_at, but does not identify each rotate/revoke actor/action.
groups.actor: Store rotate/revoke accept ID only; created_by is the original creator, not the rotating/revoking actor.
groups.identity: Token ID + from/to row versions + shared revision; rotate and revoke are not distinguished by resource_type alone; no operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2: thread mutation actor/action through ServiceTokenStore and both adapters, add immutable evidence in existing PostgreSQL transaction; preserve repeat-revoke and races.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: SQLite token mutex protects a read-time revoked guard, then an UPDATE and reload; no separate evidence transaction. The mutation SQL itself is keyed by ID.
groups.record: Current hash/revoked_at replaces earlier state; creator remains unchanged.
groups.actor: Mutation store takes token ID only; rotating/revoking actor exists in post-write HTTP telemetry.
groups.identity: Token ID, current timestamp; no persisted operation or revision chain.
groups.follow_up: PR4: same SQLite transaction for guarded token update and evidence, with actor context from shared interface; no events for ineffective repeated revoke.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: CLI revoke-jwt -> PostgresJwtRevocationStore::revoke; revoke row, shared revision and outbox commit together; already-effective duplicate rolls back reserved revision.
groups.record: Outbox keeps scoped JTI digest/revision; revocation row actor can be overwritten when extension/reactivation occurs and row is deleted after expiry.
groups.actor: CLI persists literal operator:revoke-jwt (system action, not authenticated human identity). Store supports actor_user_id but prior actor is not retained through later changes/cleanup.
groups.identity: Deployment+issuer-scoped JTI digest and security revision; outbox to_version=1 is not a per-JWT version chain; no operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2: immutable bounded revocation event in existing transaction, retain action/scoped operator provenance after expiry cleanup; no raw JTI. Do not pretend the CLI authenticates a named operator.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: CLI requires STATE_BACKEND=postgres; standalone JWT validation uses no-op revocation store.
groups.record: No standalone JWT revocation authority.
groups.actor: Not applicable.
groups.identity: Not applicable.
groups.follow_up: Keep required-durability JWT revocation unsupported until an actual standalone authority and atomic evidence exist.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: Config::from_env startup validation selects authorities; serving bootstrap assembles runtime state. PostgreSQL document seeding uses normal document commits but does not establish a revisioned whole-configuration authority.
groups.record: No common configuration activation manifest/event transaction. File/environment configuration remains operator-owned; revisioned policy/tools records cover only their own resources.
groups.actor: Startup system process; no authenticated changing operator.
groups.identity: No authoritative whole-configuration operation/revision identity.
groups.follow_up: #242 configuration ledger/activation contract first; bind validated safe manifest digest, parent revision, activation intent/result and required evidence before enabling required-durability configuration activation. Never hash/export raw secrets as a substitute for redaction.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: No unified revision-ledger configuration export/release operation is shipped. import::exports builds internal canonical projections for import comparisons; it is not a redacted configuration-export authority.
groups.record: No atomic export-intent/release record or whole-configuration manifest.
groups.actor: No configuration-export actor contract.
groups.identity: No authoritative export operation/artifact identity.
groups.follow_up: #242/#425 PR4: define authorized redacted artifact release bound to ledger revision, artifact digest and durable export event before release; keep unsupported. Internal import projections include sensitive state and must never become authority-event payloads.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: import-standalone apply is offline and commits each section separately. Policy/tools activation reuse document transactions; Connection/token imports preserve state and intentionally do not replay old outbox entries.
groups.record: Imported durable state and policy/tools activation records; JSON stdout report carries section counts/checksums. The entire import/report has no single transaction or immutable operator-operation ledger.
groups.actor: IMPORT_ACTOR marks migration provenance; historic actors retained for imported policy history. It is not authenticated human attribution.
groups.identity: Natural-key idempotence per section and canonical checksums support resume; report has no persisted whole-import operation ID.
groups.follow_up: Treat import as multiple section operations: persist resumable section evidence with each owning transaction and a final verified manifest. Retain existing no-replay outbox semantics; do not publish sensitive canonical export bodies as evidence.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: import-standalone targets PostgreSQL; a standalone configuration is only its source.
groups.record: No standalone import target operation.
groups.actor: Not applicable.
groups.identity: Not applicable.
groups.follow_up: Keep unsupported; do not infer a reverse import or merge operation from canonical comparison exports.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.
